basis: Immune-mediated epidermal and oral mucosal necrosis define SJS; lasting ocular damage and other visceral injury are occasional in supplied HPO data.
Infection-associated glomerular inflammation; the associated endocarditis is a separate disease, so no cardiovascular label.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect with common encephalopathy, developmental impairment and brain degeneration (>30%); cardiac findings in 1/2 do not establish a general frequency.
Intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; hypogonadism is a defining endocrine feature. Minor craniofacial and ear dysmorphism adds no functional axis.
Intestinal acanthocephalan infection; worms attach to and injure the intestinal wall.
Congenital thyroid dysgenesis and hypothyroidism; cardiac findings occur in 1/4, and neurologic damage lacks a qualifying frequency.
The definition specifies nasopharyngeal carcinoma despite the susceptibility wording; nasopharynx belongs to the airway axis.
Defined by pathological innate immune signaling with autoimmune and neurological disease; other organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Pneumococcal infection directly involves the intervertebral disc; the organism's name does not imply lung involvement.
Mandibulofacial dysostosis and conductive deafness define the syndrome; eyelid coloboma occurs in 2/3 and cleft palate in 1/2.
Craniofacial skeletal defects and ID define it; severe hypermetropia 80–99%, hypothyroidism 30–79%. Cap omits oral defects, ear malformations and less-specific cardiac anomalies.
Leukodystrophy, acquired microcephaly and severe developmental impairment define CNS disease; hypotonia and nystagmus do not establish separate muscle or eye damage.
Orf is a zoonotic poxvirus infection producing localized cutaneous lesions in humans.
Mature T-cell lymphoma arising around a breast implant; lymphoma warrants blood-cell and immune axes despite its breast-associated location.
Severe intellectual disability with structural CNS anomalies and acromegaly with abnormal growth hormone secretion define the syndrome.
PXDN-related anterior segment malformation causes corneal opacity, cataract and visual impairment; abnormalities are confined to the ocular axis.
Recurrent eyelid edema produces eyelid tissue atrophy and laxity; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Destructive intracerebral cavities cause neurological impairment; spasticity and hemiparesis reflect brain injury rather than primary muscle damage.
Bilateral labyrinthine dysfunction is an inner-ear vestibular disorder.
Upper and lower motor neuron disease causes spastic paraplegia and distal neurogenic amyotrophy; muscle wasting is secondary to denervation.
Compression neuropathy of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve; sensory symptoms in the thigh do not indicate skin disease.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Mature B-cell lymphoma; stomach, lung, skin and ocular involvement are subtype-specific and do not qualify across the umbrella.
Circumferential scleral ectasia is a structural disorder of the eye.
Corrosive exposure causes skin necrosis; absorbed toxin disrupts cellular metabolism with lactic acidosis. Neurologic, cardiac and renal injury lack established ≥30% frequencies.
